answer.decision: Adopt a managed search service behind an internal abstraction and portable index pipeline.
answer.action: Implement a vendor-neutral canonical search document, isolate vendor APIs behind an internal search interface, index through a portable pipeline, and validate bulk export plus reindexing as part of the four-month launch plan.
reasons: The managed service already supports faceting, typo tolerance, and near-real-time indexing required for launch.
Building now is unlikely to meet the deadline: the prior prototype consumed six engineer-weeks yet delivered only basic keyword search.
Managed service avoids adding the primary on-call and quarterly upgrade burden that the capacity-constrained team cannot absorb.
The projected cost is limited to 7 percent of the year-one product infrastructure budget.
Delaying for hiring would threaten the contracted design-partner expansion.
A canonical search document and documented bulk export API provide concrete foundations for migration away from the vendor.
assumptions: The managed service can satisfy required reliability, security, compliance, and latency expectations.
The four-month schedule includes enough time to build and test the abstraction, canonical document pipeline, export, and full reindex process.
Seven percent of the product infrastructure budget is financially acceptable.
Near-real-time indexing is supported at the expected launch traffic and update volume.
risks: The internal abstraction may leak vendor-specific query, ranking, faceting, or typo-tolerance behavior, making migration harder than expected.
Bulk export alone may not preserve relevance tuning, synonyms, analytics, or configuration.
Managed-service pricing could rise as traffic, document volume, or query complexity grows.
An abstraction designed too broadly could add schedule risk; it should focus on required capabilities and migration-critical boundaries.
Vendor outages or service limits could affect launch unless resilience and capacity are validated.

citations.claim: The managed service supports all launch features and provides a documented bulk export API.
The internal prototype required six engineer-weeks and still lacked typo tolerance and faceting.
Operating an open-source cluster requires primary on-call ownership and quarterly upgrades.
Year-one managed-service spending is projected at 7 percent of the product infrastructure budget.
A six-month delay would forgo a contracted design-partner expansion.
The data model can produce a vendor-neutral canonical search document.
